hints: Focus on what type of product each starting material can actually give, oxidation, ester hydrolysis and nitrile hydrolysis all behave very differently.
Notice reaction 1 starts from a secondary alcohol, so strong oxidation stops at the ketone stage and cannot extend the carbon chain to an acid.
Count the carbons in the ester and the nitrile fragments to confirm they both hydrolyse to a 5-carbon acid, then pick the combination with only those two.
walkthrough:
**Recall what pentanoic acid needs**

Think of pentanoic acid as $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$, a 5-carbon carboxylic acid. To make it we need a 5-carbon precursor that can be converted to $\text{-COOH}$.

Rule to use:
$$\text{R-COOH is formed by primary alcohol oxidation, ester hydrolysis, or nitrile hydrolysis}$$

**Test reaction 1, oxidation of pentan-2-ol**

The compound $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is pentan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. Strong oxidation with $\text{H}^+/\text{MnO}_4^-$ converts a secondary alcohol only to a ketone.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$$
So reaction 1 gives pentan-2-one, not pentanoic acid. Reaction 1 is false.

**Test reaction 2, acid hydrolysis of an ester**

$\text{CH}_3\text{OCO}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_3$ is methyl pentanoate. The $\text{-OCO-}$ link splits in dilute $\text{HCl(aq)}$ to give the acid plus the alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{OCO}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
The acid part has $1 + 3 + 1 = 5$ carbons, exactly pentanoic acid. Reaction 2 is true.

**Test reaction 3, acid hydrolysis of a nitrile**

$\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CN}$ contains $4 + 1 = 5$ carbons in total including the $\text{-CN}$ carbon. Hot aqueous acid hydrolyses $\text{-CN}$ fully to $\text{-COOH}$.

$$\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
This also gives pentanoic acid. Reaction 3 is true, so only 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 all work. Reaction 1 is the trap, a secondary alcohol cannot be oxidised to a carboxylic acid, it stops at pentan-2-one.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 work. Reaction 2 is correct, but reaction 1 is included by mistake. Students choosing this have correctly spotted ester hydrolysis but forgotten the primary versus secondary alcohol oxidation rule.
options.C: Correct. Reaction 2 (methyl pentanoate hydrolysis) and reaction 3 (pentanenitrile hydrolysis) both give the 5-carbon $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$. Reaction 1 gives only a ketone, so it is correctly excluded.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only reaction 3 works. Reaction 3 does work, but reaction 2 is missed. Students choosing this often forget that esters hydrolyse with aqueous acid to give the parent carboxylic acid plus alcohol.
